problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems struggle on structured, repetitive corpora like regulatory filings because chunk similarity alone often fails to distinguish between documents with overlapping language (p.1). Specifically, traditional vector-based retrieval lacks sufficient discriminative power for documents that follow rigid templates and reuse language, causing retrievers to return superficially relevant but unhelpful chunks (p.1-2).
methodology: The paper presents a systematic study of metadata-aware retrieval strategies, comparing a plain-text baseline with metadata-as-text (prefix and suffix), a dual-encoder unified embedding that fuses metadata and content in a single index using a weighted sum, dual-encoder late-fusion retrieval, and metadata-aware query reformulation via an LLM (p.1, 5-6). It evaluates these strategies using frozen text encoders (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small and BAAI bge-m3) and analyzes the embedding space geometry (p.7, 8).
dataset: The authors introduce RAGMATE-10K, a dataset of 25 SEC 10-K filings from five U.S. technology companies (Apple, Alphabet, Adobe, Oracle, Nvidia) segmented into 4,490 non-overlapping 350-token chunks with 50-token overlap, paired with 120 test queries after excluding Apple (p.7).
results: Metadata-enriched strategies consistently outperformed the plain baseline, with prefix-based metadata-as-text and dual-encoder unified embeddings standing out as the most effective approaches (p.9, 10). Dual-encoder unified embeddings achieved accuracy matching or surpassing prefixing while simplifying index maintenance and serving (p.9). In embedding space analysis, the mean margin between positive and negative pairs tripled from 0.054 to 0.152, Cohen's d grew from 0.45 to 2.25, and AUC rose from 0.625 to 0.94 for unified embeddings (p.11).
key_findings: Embedding metadata alongside content significantly improves retrieval performance by increasing intra-document cohesion, reducing inter-document confusion, and widening the separation between relevant and irrelevant chunks (p.1, 3, 13). Field-level ablations demonstrated that global identifiers like company and year provide strong disambiguating signals, whereas local section titles offer more modest gains (p.3, 12).
limitations: The study focuses exclusively on SEC Form 10-K filings, which are a deliberately challenging stress-test corpus, meaning absolute gains may vary across domains (p.13). Ground-truth answers were generated in a semi-supervised manner using an LLM, and the evaluation utilized frozen encoders without exploring fine-tuning or end-to-end training (p.13).
title: Utilizing Metadata for Better Retrieval-Augmented Generation
